bds.h: Dolores Huerta, labor activist and civil rights icon, dies at 96
bds.lede: Dolores Huerta was a labor activist and civil rights leader who co-founded the group that later became the United Farm Workers.
rows: CBS News
Dolores Huerta was a labor activist and civil rights leader who co-founded the group that later became the United Farm Workers.
BBC News
Huerta fought for farm workers' rights in the 1960s and 1970s and had continued to work addressing immigration and voting issues.
Times Colonist

Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase “Sí, se puede!” that became a widespread rallying cry, has died. She was 96.
The Guardian
Huerta co-founded United Farm Workers union with Cesar Chavez, improving pay and conditions for farm workers
PBS NewsHour
Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase “Sí, se puede!” that became a widespread rallying cry.
Fox News
The longtime labor organizer and civil rights activist helped build a national movement advocating for agricultural workers after beginning her career as a schoolteacher.

bds.h: Defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family land in Miami after fleeing Brazil
bds.lede: MIAMI (AP) — Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami on Wednesday after he refused to concede the election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and fled the country.
rows: Times Colonist

MIAMI (AP) — Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami on Wednesday after he refused to concede the election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and fled the country.
CTV News
Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami on Wednesday after fleeing Brazil.
BBC News
The defeated Brazilian presidential candidate arrived in the US by private jet on Tuesday morning with his wife and two daughters.
PBS NewsHour

The stunning move came after 48 hours in which Bolsonaro refused to concede to Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and then threatened to attempt to annul the election result. He is under investigation by Brazil’s Supreme Court for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion in…
Al Jazeera
Bolsonaro and his family have fled to the US amid a Brazilian Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.
CBS News
Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil's presidential election, left the country with his family and State Department official told CBS News they would receive U.S. visas.
